subject: Opposition to Local Development Projects
overview: Host John Petrella interviewed Medford resident Trish Schiapelli about her opposition to several local development projects, including a proposed methadone dispensary and the Salem Street rezoning. Schiapelli expressed concerns over the municipal administration's transparency, financial management, and community outreach.

items.title: Introduction of Guest
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced guest Trish Schiapelli to discuss current issues affecting the city of Medford.

items.title: Opposition to Proposed Methadone Dispensary
items.summary: Schiapelli explained that her involvement in local issues began after discovering a proposed methadone dispensary was planned near an elementary school on Salem Street.

items.title: Critique of City Council and Administration
items.summary: Schiapelli criticized the City Council and administration, alleging a lack of business experience and a pattern of block voting.

items.title: Community Mobilization and Legal Representation
items.summary: Schiapelli discussed gathering petitions against the methadone dispensary and hiring an attorney specializing in municipal law to represent concerned residents.

items.title: Salem Street Rezoning Opposition
items.summary: Schiapelli detailed community resistance to the Salem Street rezoning, pointing to a lack of traffic studies and deficient outreach in an environmental justice neighborhood.

items.title: Other City Development Projects
items.summary: Schiapelli voiced concerns regarding other concurrent developments, including a proposed 10-story Tufts University dormitory in South Medford.

items.title: Financial Management and Municipal Concerns
items.summary: Schiapelli called for municipal audits and criticized city financial management, specifically citing $9 million left in a non-interest-bearing checking account.
